findings.description: When the target already exists, the function returns early without removing the temp file in incoming/. Each duplicate upload leaves a full-size orphan file behind, so disk usage grows unboundedly with repeated uploads of the same content.
findings.suggestion: Call incoming.unlink(missing_ok=True) before returning when target.exists(). Also wrap the mkdir/os.replace step in try/except to unlink the temp file on failure.
findings.title: Temp upload file leaked when blob already exists

findings.description: The cleanup try/except only covers the write loop. If target.parent.mkdir or os.replace raises (permissions, disk error, ENOSPC), the temp file stays in incoming/ forever.
findings.suggestion: Extend the try/except to include the finalize step, or use a finally that unlinks incoming with missing_ok=True.
findings.title: Temp file leaked if mkdir or os.replace fails

findings.description: Incoming dir is under root, which is fine for same-filesystem rename, but the old mkdir of root is now only implicit. More importantly the blob layout uses two-hex-char directories; 'incoming' does not collide. However no durability: data is not fsynced before os.replace, so a crash can leave a zero-length or truncated blob at the final content-addressed path, which is then treated as existing and never repaired.
findings.suggestion: Call out.flush() and os.fsync(out.fileno()) before closing, prior to os.replace.
findings.title: Root directory collides with 'incoming' digest prefix namespace and may break rename across filesystems
